l4_steps.name: Extract technical delay & cancellation events
l4_steps.input: Daily operations data feeds, PIREP submissions, MEL deferrals
l4_steps.output: Reliability event log with ATA chapter coding
l4_steps.pain_point: AMOS data quality degrades at outstations using paper-based PIREP capture; electronic sync lags up to 24 hours, distorting daily reliability figures

l4_steps.name: Compile PIREP and cabin defect report data
l4_steps.input: Pilot reports (PIREPs), cabin defect logs, maintenance findings
l4_steps.output: Consolidated defect database partitioned by ATA chapter
l4_steps.kpi: Repeat defect rate <2% per ATA chapter per month
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent ATA chapter coding across maintenance bases causes mis-classification; repeat defects counted under different chapters, masking true recurrence rates

l4_steps.name: Calculate ATA chapter reliability metrics
l4_steps.input: AMOS defect export, flight operations hours and cycles data
l4_steps.output: ATA chapter reliability scorecard (events per 1,000 flight hours)
l4_steps.kpi: Alert threshold: >3 events / 1,000 flight hours per ATA chapter triggers review
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual data extraction from AMOS via CSV export introduces processing lag of 2–3 days; no real-time API feed from AMOS to BI platform

l4_steps.name: Assess alert threshold breach and escalate
l4_steps.output: Alert notification issued to MRB, or threshold cleared and monitoring continues
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of threshold breaches assessed within 2 business days of month-end data close
l4_steps.pain_point: Alert threshold logic embedded in legacy spreadsheets not integrated with AMOS or Redshift; threshold parameters updated manually and inconsistently across fleet types

l4_steps.name: Initiate formal failure investigation record
l4_steps.input: Alert notification from MRB, repeat defect flag
l4_steps.output: Investigation record opened in AMOS with case owner assigned
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of Level 1 alert items investigated within 5 business days of alert
l4_steps.pain_point: Insufficient root cause data available when aircraft operated at remote outstations; maintenance findings not captured in AMOS before aircraft repositions

l4_steps.name: Perform MSG-3 logic and FMEA assessment
l4_steps.input: Failure investigation record, OEM Maintenance Planning Document (MPD)
l4_steps.output: FMEA worksheet with failure mode, cause, and effect documented
l4_steps.kpi: FMEA completed for 100% of Level 1 alert items within investigation SLA
l4_steps.pain_point: Boeing Toolbox concurrent-user licence constraints limit simultaneous FMEA sessions; engineers queue for access during peak investigation periods, extending cycle time

l4_steps.name: Classify failure consequence category
l4_steps.input: FMEA worksheet, MPD task data, airworthiness directive index
l4_steps.output: Failure consequence classification: Safety / Operational / Economic / Hidden
l4_steps.kpi: 100% classification accuracy validated by MRB at monthly review
l4_steps.pain_point: Safety consequences misclassified as operational when CAMP airworthiness data is stale due to deferred AD entry; classification errors trigger rework and regulatory exposure

l4_steps.name: Identify and document corrective task recommendation
l4_steps.input: Failure consequence classification, OEM service bulletin index
l4_steps.output: Task change recommendation record with justification and urgency rating
l4_steps.kpi: Recommendation issued within 10 business days of alert escalation
l4_steps.pain_point: OEM (Boeing/Airbus) response SLA for MPD revision guidance averages 45 days, creating a backlog of open recommendations awaiting OEM concurrence before implementation

l4_steps.name: Evaluate existing MPD task applicability
l4_steps.input: Task change recommendation, current approved MPD tasks
l4_steps.output: Task gap analysis identifying intervals to extend, reduce, or replace
l4_steps.kpi: Task revision scope defined within 5 business days of recommendation receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Mixed 737-700/800/MAX fleet requires parallel MPD analysis tracks; task applicability differs by line number and engine variant, increasing analysis effort by 30–40%

l4_steps.name: Develop revised maintenance task intervals
l4_steps.input: Task gap analysis, reliability trend data, Weibull statistical model output
l4_steps.output: Draft task card revision with updated intervals (FH / FC / calendar)
l4_steps.kpi: Interval extension justified at ≥95% statistical confidence using Weibull analysis
l4_steps.pain_point: Small fleet sample size for 737 MAX subtype (<50 aircraft in some configurations) limits Weibull confidence; task intervals set conservatively, missing potential cost optimisation

l4_steps.name: Assess regulatory change approval requirement
l4_steps.input: Draft task card revision, FAR Part 121.370 compliance matrix
l4_steps.output: Regulatory assessment memo classifying change as self-approval or FSDO submission
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of safety-consequence task changes submitted for FAA/EASA regulatory review
l4_steps.pain_point: Ambiguity in FAR 121.370 on what constitutes a 'significant' maintenance program change requires legal review for borderline cases, adding 5–10 days to the cycle

l4_steps.name: Issue Engineering Order or Maintenance Program Amendment
l4_steps.input: Approved task revision, regulatory assessment memo
l4_steps.output: Engineering Order (EO) or Maintenance Program Amendment (MPA) document
l4_steps.kpi: Engineering Order issued within 15 business days of task approval
l4_steps.pain_point: Concurrent EO backlog regularly exceeds 60 open items; engineering resource constraint delays issuance and causes task cards to remain at superseded intervals in production

l4_steps.name: Submit MPA to FAA FSDO or EASA for approval
l4_steps.input: Maintenance Program Amendment with supporting FMEA and reliability data
l4_steps.output: Regulatory submission package with acknowledgement reference number
l4_steps.kpi: FAA approval turnaround ≤90 days for non-safety items per FAR 121.370
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA FSDO staffing shortages in 2024–2025 causing MPA approval delays beyond 120 days for complex amendments; aircraft continue operating on superseded intervals during review

l4_steps.name: Update approved task cards in AMOS
l4_steps.input: Regulatory approval letter or self-approval sign-off, approved MPA
l4_steps.output: Updated task cards activated in AMOS with new intervals and applicability
l4_steps.kpi: 100% task card accuracy post-update verified by QA within 48 hours of activation
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual task card entry in AMOS prone to interval transcription errors (confusing FH vs FC vs calendar values); errors not caught until next scheduled QA audit cycle

l4_steps.name: Validate task card update accuracy via QA audit
l4_steps.input: Updated AMOS task cards, approved MPA source document
l4_steps.output: QA sign-off record or discrepancy report requiring correction
l4_steps.kpi: Zero task card interval discrepancies at post-update audit; 100% of failed audits remediated within 5 days
l4_steps.pain_point: QA audit sampling rate of 10% for low-risk task revisions may miss low-frequency task card errors on infrequently performed tasks until first work-order execution

l4_steps.name: Train maintenance technicians on revised tasks
l4_steps.input: Approved revised task cards, training needs analysis
l4_steps.output: Training completion records with competency sign-off per technician
l4_steps.kpi: 100% technician training completion within 30 days of task implementation
l4_steps.pain_point: SAP SuccessFactors LMS is not integrated with the AMOS task library; training content must be manually synced, leading to version mismatches between LMS materials and live task cards

l4_steps.name: Generate monthly reliability performance report
l4_steps.input: AMOS reliability data export, flight operations performance data
l4_steps.output: Monthly Reliability Report (MRR) with ATA trend charts and open action items
l4_steps.kpi: Report published within 5 business days of month-end data close
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual consolidation of AMOS export and ops data in spreadsheets creates version control risk; no automated pipeline from AMOS to Tableau, requiring 2–3 days of analyst effort per cycle

l4_steps.name: Present findings to Maintenance Review Board
l4_steps.input: Monthly Reliability Report, open investigation items
l4_steps.output: MRB minutes with closed actions and new action items assigned
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of open MRB action items tracked to closure within agreed timescales; MRB held monthly
l4_steps.pain_point: MRB meeting cadence slips during heavy maintenance check periods; unresolved reliability actions go untracked for up to 60 days, breaching IATA Maintenance Review Board guidelines

l4_steps.name: Assess corrective action effectiveness and close investigation
l4_steps.input: MRB minutes, post-change reliability trend data (90-day lookback)
l4_steps.output: Investigation closure record or re-escalation trigger for repeat failure
l4_steps.kpi: Recurrence rate <5% within 90 days of corrective action implementation
l4_steps.pain_point: Corrective action effectiveness undermined when task changes are not adopted uniformly across all maintenance bases; partial implementation creates split-fleet reliability data that masks recurrence
